Approved findings

Approved evidence · As of 12 Nov 2026

surge riemann · evaluates: Riemann-Bench’s v3 paper permits coding and search tools with no token-budget/interaction-format constraints and describes one hundred independent attempts per model/problem for pass@k estimation.

Permanent record ID: candidate.add17.riemann.evaluation.v2

  • The blog body retains an earlier one-hour timeout while its update note removes that limit; those conflicting time-budget scopes are preserved without selecting a favorable performance number.

Approved evidence · As of 12 Nov 2026

surge riemann · human annotation: Riemann-Bench’s v3 paper describes twenty-five research-level mathematics problems drawn by active mathematicians from their own work, with definite verifiable answers requiring extended theoretical reasoning.

Permanent record ID: candidate.add17.riemann.problem-origin.v2

  • The problems have known solutions; they are not themselves open conjectures such as the Riemann hypothesis.

Approved evidence · As of 12 Nov 2026

surge riemann · has stage: Riemann-Bench’s paper requires two independent domain experts to solve each problem from scratch without seeing the author’s solution, checking ambiguity, underspecification anddifficulty, with revision or removal after failed verification.

Permanent record ID: candidate.add17.riemann.verification.v2

  • The benchmark’s double-blind verification is its reported construction protocol, not an independent peer decision on this research claim.
